title: Enhancing Lossy Compression Through Cross-Field Information for Scientific Applications
problem: Lossy compression of multi-field scientific data is limited by existing approaches that use only local information from a single target field when predicting target data points, restricting achievable compression ratios.
motivation: Effective lossy compression of large-scale scientific datasets is critical for reducing data size and enabling efficient storage and transmission.
method: The paper proposes a hybrid prediction model using Convolutional Neural Networks to extract cross-field correlations and combines this information with local field information. These enhanced predictions improve prediction accuracy for lossy compressors to achieve better compression ratios.
key_novelty: Leveraging CNN-extracted cross-field correlations within scientific datasets to enhance lossy compression prediction accuracy beyond single-field local information.
contributions: Identified significant cross-field correlations in multi-field scientific datasets
Developed a hybrid prediction model combining CNN-based cross-field information with local field information
Demonstrated up to 25% compression ratio improvement under specific error bounds
Achieved improved data detail preservation and reduced artifacts compared to baseline approaches

metrics.accuracy: Compression ratio improved by up to 25%; data details preserved with reduced artifacts

limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Cross-field information for enhanced lossy compression
